comparison: Perfect agreement on genome assembly quality (C1-C10). Both evaluations find the assembly well-supported and valuable, with OpenEval providing technical validation of metrics and peer reviewers recognizing it as a strategic resource.

Strong agreement on transcriptomic findings (C11-C20, C22). Both support the developmental phase identification and gene expression patterns. OpenEval notes the novelty claim (C22) may be overstated without systematic review, while peer reviewers implicitly accept it as a 'significant advance.' Peer review does not address C21 comparison claim.

Strong agreement on TH pathway activation (C23-C35, C39-C40). Both recognize the early TH event as novel and well-documented. OpenEval notes temporal resolution limitations in hormone measurements, while peer reviewers emphasize the work's contribution to understanding thyroid signaling. Peer review does not separately address C36-C38 metamorphosis correlation.

Both address TH activation timing and metamorphosis correlation (C36-C38). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of TH pathway genes and hormone measurements, while peer reviewers accept the correlation between TH and metamorphic changes as part of the broader developmental analysis. Also includes C21 comparison to other groupers.

Divergent evaluations on spine formation claims (C41-C45). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing the speculative nature of TH regulation inference based solely on temporal correlation without functional validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the correlation as part of the comprehensive developmental analysis without challenging the mechanistic inference.

Complete agreement on pigmentation gene expression (C46-C51). Both evaluations support the descriptive findings and accept the correlations as appropriately speculative. OpenEval emphasizes observational nature, while peer reviewers accept as part of comprehensive developmental resources.

Complete agreement on opsin expression patterns (C52-C60). Both support the data and comparisons to other species. OpenEval notes that photoreceptor differentiation inferences would benefit from histological validation, while peer reviewers accept findings without specific critique.

Complete agreement on metabolic gene expression (C61-C71). Both support the documented patterns and metabolic shift interpretation. OpenEval emphasizes that TH regulation speculation (C69-C70) requires experimental validation, while peer reviewers accept the cautiously presented findings as part of the developmental analysis.

Partial agreement on corticoid pathway activation (C72-C81, C90). Both support the gene expression data and cortisol measurements. OpenEval rates overall as UNCERTAIN due to speculative TH-corticoid synergy (C91), while peer reviewers rate the basic corticoid activation as SUPPORTED but separately address the crosstalk hypothesis.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding TH-corticoid crosstalk (C82-C89, C91-C92, C116-C119). Both evaluations recognize this as speculative, based on temporal correlation and literature from other species without functional validation. OpenEval and peer reviewers both note the need for experimental testing.

Agreement on pigmentation alternative explanation (C93-C95). OpenEval includes this as part of broader corticoid analysis rated UNCERTAIN, while peer reviewers separately support it as a plausible alternative interpretation, though both recognize it remains speculative.

Strong agreement on synthesis and model system proposal (C96-C99, C132). Both evaluations support the identification of a novel ontogenetic transition and the value of E. malabaricus as a model. Peer reviewers emphasize this as a 'significant advance,' while OpenEval notes the hypothesis requires further validation.

Partial overlap on background claims (C100-C131 in OpenEval vs C116-C119 in peer review). Both support the characterization of knowledge gaps regarding corticoid-TH interactions in fish. OpenEval addresses broader background context that peer reviewers do not separately evaluate.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background claims (C100-C115, C120-C131) regarding grouper biology, aquaculture importance, and TH/corticoid pathway roles. No corresponding separate peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers implicitly accept the study rationale.
